articles.body:

articles.title: Save $40 Off Microsoft's Professional-Grade Xbox Elite Series 2 Core Wireless Controller
articles.summary: Worth the upgrade.
articles.body:
Do you prefer PlayStation or Xbox controllers? I'm in the latter camp. My favorite PC controllers have always been modeled after Xbox's tried and true asymmetrical layout. And when it comes to Xbox controllers, you can't get much better than the highest end model from Microsoft itself. For a limited time, Amazon is offering the professional-grade Xbox Series X Elite Series 2 Core Wireless Controller for $109.99 with free shipping. It's currently $150 everywhere else.

The Elite Series 2 Core is the official premium controller for Xbox. The Core model is physically identical to the previous generation $200 Xbox Elite Series 2 controller, with integrated pro gaming features like adjustable-tension thumbsticks, wrap-around rubberized grip, and shorter hair trigger locks. The only difference is that the original Elite controller comes with more accessories: extra sets of paddles, thumbsticks, D-pad, and a travel case. The Elite Series 2 Core doesn't come with any of those accessories. You can buy them separately as a component pack for $59.99.

I'm not very optimistic, however, that the launch price will be the same as the Xbox Series 2 controller when it first released at $179.99. articles.title: The Batman Part 2 Brings in Director Steven Soderbergh to Finish Film in Place of Matt Reeves
articles.summary: Ocean's 11 director Steven Soderbergh has been hired to finish filming The Batman Part 2 while Matt Reeves attends to a family matter.
articles.body:
UPDATE: Matt Reeves has released his own statement, confirming that he is still very much apart of the film's produciton and is not leaving the project.

"Just to be clear, I am not leaving The Batman Part II," said Reeves . "I am profoundly grateful to Steven for coming to my aid during this challenging time to help me finish principal photography. Thank you to all for your concern and well wishes."

Ocean's 11 director Steven Soderbergh has been hired to finish filming The Batman Part II while Matt Reeves attends to a family matter.

It was reported earlier this month that The Batman Part II director Matt Reeves was abruptly stepping away from the project to attend to personal matters. This left the film in a strange state of limbo, but DC boss Peter Safran recently told IGN that the project would be finished . Now we know how. Warner Bros. confirmed to Deadline that Ocean's 11 director Steven Soderbergh will helm and complete the superhero sequel during its final weeks of production.

“As Matt Reeves continues to attend to an ongoing family matter, Steven Soderbergh, as an admirer of Matt’s work, approached Matt and will step in to help the writer-director complete the final weeks of principal photography on The Batman Part II," a WB rep told Deadline. "Matt and Steven will work closely together with the actors and crew to fulfill Matt’s vision of the film.”

The Batman: Part II - Who's Who in Matt Reeves' DC Sequel

Soderbergh is working directly with Matt Reeves during this process, with Deadline reporter Justin Kroll noting that Reeves is working on the film remotely from his home. Once the movie is wrapped, Soderbergh will hand things back over to Reeves so he can handle the post-production process. The goal is to finish Reeves' original vision for the sequel as opposed to having Soderbergh do something radically different.

“I thought Matt Reeves’ work on The Batman was stunning; it was intentional, specific, and rigorously coherent," said Soderbergh. "The goal here is to work with Matt and his team to generate footage that will integrate seamlessly with what’s already been shot so Matt can properly finish his film.”

As of right now, it's unclear if the stoppage will lead to another delay. The Batman Part II has already been pushed back several times and is currently due out February 2028 . Given it's expected that there isn't too much left to shoot on the movie, this may not create any significant setbacks.

Soderbergh is a pretty efficent director, often handling multiple production roles himself. He's known for having a firm handle on budgets and being able to shoot quickly, which is something that the studio will likely greatly appreciate in this situation. He also has an Oscar for Best Director, which gives him an extra degree of prestige.

The Batman Part II is currently slated to hit theaters on February 18, 2028.

articles.title: The Fourth Wing TV Series Has Reportedly Found Its Xaden and Violet
articles.summary: Prime Video's adaptation of the best-selling romantasy series, Fourth Wing, has reportdely found its stars. Esther McGregor has been cast as Violet Sorrengail and Emilio Sakraya will be taking on the role of Zaden Riorson.
articles.body:
Prime Video's adaptation of the best-selling romantasy series , Fourth Wing, has reportdely found its stars. Esther McGregor has been cast as Violet Sorrengail and Emilio Sakraya will be taking on the role of Zaden Riorson.

The news arrived earlier today via Deadline stating that the two actors have been confirmed. This is the first casting news we've received about the highly anticipated adaptation, and it's the most impactful. The heart of Rebecca Yarros' steamy fantasy romance series is the relationship between these two characters, so their performance will make or break the series.

Prime Video has found its leading stars for ‘Fourth Wing,’ the TV series adaptation of Rebecca Yarros’ bestselling novel. Esther McGregor has been cast as Violet Sorrengail, and Emilio Sakraya will bring to life the character of Xaden Riorson, sources close to production tell Deadline. More details here: — Deadline (@DEADLINE) October 15, 2026

Prime Video has found its leading stars for ‘Fourth Wing,’ the TV series adaptation of Rebecca Yarros’ bestselling novel. Esther McGregor has been cast as Violet Sorrengail, and Emilio Sakraya will bring to life the character of Xaden Riorson, sources close to production tell Deadline. More details here:

You may know Esther McGregor for her role as Isabel in A24's Baby Girl , where she worked alongside Nicole Kidman and Antonio Banderas. She also appeared in an episode of Obi-Wan Kenobi as Tetha Grig, a pink-haired spice dealer, which is notable because she is in fact Ewan McGregor's daughter.

Emilio Sakraya is perhaps most well-known for his depiction of ex-con Giwar Hajabi in the 2022 film Rheingold. You may also know him from his stint as JC in the first season of Netflix's Warrior Nun series .

For those not already familiar with the Fourth Wing books (AKA the Empyrean series), let's quickly break down who these characters are: Violet Sorrengail is the main protagonist in the books and is often referenced as a beautiful but frail girl with a deadly side to her. Xaden Riorsen is portrayed as a dark, powerful, and misunderstood guy with too many secrets. Both of these characters attend Basgiath War College where they learn to control powers given to them by massive dragons.

Whether or not these actors can accurately portray these two characters remains to be seen, but they definitely appear to fit their book descriptions. Seeing as this is the most important relationship in the series, they will need to have very good chemistry to be able to portray the love/hate relationship that makes the first Fourth Wing book so good.

The Fourth Wing TV series does not currently have a release date attached, but we do already know that Meredith Averill is serving as showrunner and executive producer. Rebecca Yarros will also be an executive producer on the project alongside Michael B. Jordan's Outlier Society.

While fans are waiting for the TV adaptation to become a reality, Rebecca Yarros is currently working on book four of the series. She's also been collaborating on several tabletop adaptations for the franchise as popularity continues to grow. Most recently, Yarros released Threshing Day , a standalone novel depicting the perspectives of various other characters on the day they got their dragons.

articles.title: Remedy Boss Reacts After Control Resonant Sells 1 Million Copies, Becoming Studio's Fastest-Selling Game
articles.summary: Control Resonant has sold one million copies, becoming Remedy’s fastest-selling game in spite of leakers cracking the title and pirating it after its digital launch in September.
articles.body:
Control Resonant has sold one million copies, becoming Remedy’s fastest-selling game in spite of leakers cracking the title and pirating it after its digital launch in September.

Remedy celebrated this milestone on October 15, writing on Twitter/X, “Thank you for the support. For playing, sharing, and being a part of the community.”

Remedy’s communications director Thomas Puha also commented on this achievement, saying, “There we go. Strong start.”

There we go. Strong start. — Thomas Puha (@RiotRMD) October 15, 2026

This means that Control Resonant has soared past Alan Wake 2 , which previously held the record for the studio’s fastest-selling title. The legacy sequel reached one million copies sold two months after its release; Control Resonant has achieved that figure in just three weeks.

This is welcome news for both Remedy and fans of the game, many of whom urged players against downloading the pirated version of the title when it launched digitally in late September. It seems this wasn’t a crippling setback for the developer, though, given its current financial success — and physical editions of the game have just now been released, so there’s still more profit to be had.

Control Resonant was met with critical acclaim among both reviewers and players alike. We at IGN scored it an eight out of 10 , with reviewer Michael Higham saying, “Even when combat's sharp edge eventually dulls, Control Resonant is a great addition to the Remedyverse. While its story follows a more standard framework, its gravitational pull is in the inventive world built around it and the humanization that grounds the paranatural intrigue.”

In fact, the game was so good that many internet pirates decided against illegally downloading it, choosing instead to support Remedy in the hopes that its success would help keep the studio alive.

"One of the very few games I'm going to be buying, Remedy are on the brink of bankruptcy, this is their make or break title, I love their games and gotta do what I can to keep them afloat," wrote one fan on a piracy subreddit.

"I wasn't planning to buy it but now I feel like I should," another said. "I like Remedy. They do good games."

Remedy is known for titles like the original Control game, Alan Wake 2, Max Payne , and Quantum Break . And while their offerings have been met with high praise from players, they aren’t necessarily tailored for mass appeal, leaving some gamers worried about the developer’s future — but if these latest figures are anything to go by, it seems to be faring just fine.

articles.title: Does the Vision Feel Abandoned by the Avengers? ‘I Think So,’ Says Paul Bettany
articles.summary: VisionQuest stars Paul Bettany and James Spader on the father-son dynamic behind the new MCU series, the lack of Avengers, Ultron's feelings about Wanda, and more.
articles.body:
It’s been almost five years since we last saw the Vision in WandaVision, but now he’s back – or a version of him is, anyway – in the new Disney+ series VisionQuest . Paul Bettany returns as the android (synthezoid for you Marvel heads) alongside James Spader’s Ultron and a variety of other AIs from the MCU, including JARVIS (James D'Arcy), FRIDAY (Orla Brady), and EDITH (Emily Hampshire).

But you know who’s not present for the new show? Wanda Maximoff or the Avengers. That doesn’t come as much of a surprise considering that Wanda (Elizabeth Olsen) is, well, dead after the events of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness , and the Avengers just aren’t themselves these days, what with there apparently being two teams floating around the MCU right now (which none of the original members are a part of).

Notably, in the VisionQuest premiere, Vision muses to himself about how he seems to have evaded everyone who’s been looking for him since the events of WandaVision. “There isn’t an enemy, an acquaintance… or even an Avenger trying to find the Vision,” he says. But when he says this line, Bettany delivers it with a sort of melancholy realization. So of course I had to ask the actor about it when we spoke recently – specifically if Vision feels abandoned by the Avengers in that moment.

“Well, I think so,” Bettany explains. “I finally realized that I was really making Vision for a version of me as a child, where I felt like the outsider who was bullied. I didn't think I would ever fit in anywhere. So it's just a moment to remind [us]... It's sitting on a chair at a dance, a school dance, you know what I mean? And having the courage to go and talk to a girl.”

And then there’s the Wanda of it all. Somehow I doubt there’s a single Marvel fan out there who thinks the Scarlet Witch is really, truly dead, despite the whole Mount Wundagore falling on top of her thing in Doctor Strange 2. At this point in the series, Vision (formerly known as White Vision, who lacked the emotions and memories of the original Vision before meeting a magical version of the OG back in WandaVision – it was a whole thing) is detached from humanity, as well as any deep feelings about Wanda (or at least that’s how he’s presenting). But how about Ultron, the now-imprisoned villain who Wanda and her late brother Pietro (Aaron Taylor-Johnson) once worked for? What are his thoughts on the Vision’s former partner and the mother of their children?

“He's pretty rude about Wanda,” Spader tells me. Essentially, Wanda is dead now, and so for Ultron she doesn’t matter anymore. “Ultron lives in the present. He really lives in the present. And he's ready to step forward. And he's not going to step forward until he shoves [Vision] ahead of him.”

Regarding the relationship between Vision and Ultron, while when we first meet him here, Ultron is trapped in the artificial reality that Vision has constructed, the two clearly have an important bond. “He's sort of like a quasi-therapist, psychotic father figure,” Bettany says of Spader’s character.

“I think without question, he looks at him as a son-like figure,” says Spader. “It serves him well to perceive him as that. ... But I think the more interesting thing is how much it matters to him how Vision perceives him. And it's touching in a way because he … allows himself to not care or to appear to not care, but he does. He really does care. But what's interesting is it's not so much he cares how he feels about Vision. It's he really cares about how Vision perceives him.”

Fans will recall the great scene between Vision and Ultron from Avengers: Age of Ultron, where the two synthetic lifeforms discussed humanity – both the pros and the cons of the species. It was that scene – which Spader points out was actually filmed in a parking lot and not a forest as it appears to be in the final film – which really is a key to why Ultron is back for VisionQuest, and what the relationship between the two characters is all about.

“It's this little seed of the last scene with them in Age of Ultron,” says Spader. “[We] grew it and watered it and fed it and raised it and gave it light and it blossomed into this amazing show and story. And these characters, they came from this seed, but they grow into this fabulous thing, this fabulous creation [that's] funny and moving and sad and tragic and incredibly exciting and thrilling and disturbing at times.”

In that scene from 11 years ago, Vision says the following to the defeated Ultron:

“Humans are odd. They think order and chaos are somehow opposites, and try to control what won't be. But there is grace in their failings. I think you missed that.”

Says Spader, “He spends 13 years really embracing that idea and really embracing humanity because of that idea. Where it's him. He is chaos. That's what he is. That's what he lives for. That's who he is. And yet his son is dedicated at this present time to trying to find order and trying to process this. And what they then learn from one another is fabulous and funny and exciting and challenging for both of them. And they both get as much from each other as the other.”

The actors also think that there’s been a shift of perspective for Vision since Age of Ultron in that the events since that film – when Viz was, don’t forget, just born yesterday – have caused the android to have “very real doubts” and be confused by the chaos of the world, and more specifically, the chaos that humanity brings.

“But it's funny, the two of them are very different,” continues Spader. “Vision has a sense of consequences and has a sense of collateral effect that I don't think Ultron... Ultron just wants more. And I don't think he thinks about the consequences. I think he accepts chaos in all its forms and therefore … the dichotomy between their two reactions, and how it comes together, they force it together.”

VisionQuest is streaming on Disney+ now.

articles.title: Rep. Ritchie Torres Introduces Legislation to Ensure Gamers Own Their Digital Games
articles.summary: Democratic Congressman Ritchie Torres is introducing legislation that aims to ensure you own your digital games, rather than having a license.
articles.body:
Democratic Congressman Ritchie Torres is introducing legislation that aims to ensure you own your digital games, rather than merely buying a license that gives you permission to play them.

The bill, known as The Power to the Players Act, would direct the Fedral Trade Commission (FTC) to establish regulations that would protect gamers and their digital libraries. In short, Torres wants to ensure that when you buy a digital game, you actually own it, as opposed to getting a license that can be revoked. Additionally, the bill would require online games to have offline functionality, so that when servers are shut down, the content can still be played by those who own the game.

“Consumers must have the right to own, the right to play, and the right to transfer the games they buy,” Torres said in a press release . “A game that can be taken away the moment a company pulls the plug is not a purchase. It is a rental disguised as a sale. Families in the Bronx and across the country save up to buy these games, and they deserve better than a license that can vanish at any time. The Power To The Players Act ensures consumers own what they buy and can keep playing long after a company moves on.”

Torres made an example out of NBA 2K25, a game that recently announced that it would be rendering single-player modes inaccessible due to servers shutting down. The news gained widespread attention, as many were confused why a game that's only two years old was becoming obsolete so soon.

Torres' bill addresses ongoing controversies in the industry. Earlier this year, it was confirmed that PlayStation would be ditching physical games starting in 2028 , which would mean gamers wouldn't be able to truly own their games starting with the next-generation. GTA 6 is also skipping a physical release this November , meaning there won't be any used copies of the game following its release. It's a slippery slope, and one that gamers have been battling for some time now.

The Stop Killing Games movement has been fighting to make games more accessible to their current owners, even after they shut down servers. Torress' bill would ensure they get their way, at least in the United States. Of course, we'll have to see if this bill makes it to the finish line, but it's a noble effort and shows that someone is trying to make change happen.

articles.title: Save $900 Off the New 2026 65" Hisense UR8 RGB Mini-LED TV, One of the Best TVs You Can Get for Gaming
articles.summary: The new 2026 RGB Mini-LED tech boasts richer colors, a brighter picture, and wider viewing angles than ever before.
articles.body:
Last year, Hisense pioneered the first RGB Mini-LED TV with its 116UX model. Granted it was only available as a massive 116" screen that retailed for $20,000. In 2026, Hisense released its second generation RGB Mini-LED tech at a much more affordable price point with its UR-series lineup. Ahead of Black Friday, you can get it for even less. Best Buy has just discounted the 65" Hisense UR8 RGB Mini-LED TV from $2,000 all the way down to $1,099.99 with free shipping.

The Hisense UR8 RGB Mini-LED TV Gives OLED a Run for Its Money

RGB Mini-LED is essentially the next generation evolution of Mini-LED technology. Traditional mini-LED TVs consist of an array of blue LED that are passed through RGB filters to produced the desired color. RGB Mini-LED TVs use red, green, and blue LEDs instead of just blue, which means the pixels no longer need filters to produce the desired color. The result is more accurate color reproduction, less blooming and, most importantly, a wider color gamut. In fact, the color gamut of RGB Mini-LED surpasses that of OLEDs, since current-generation OLEDs also use color filters combined with blue OLEDs. How does that translate in the real world? It means that you see richer, more accurate colors, smoother gradients and less banding than even OLEDs, especially in 4K HDR content.

RGB Mini-LED TVs have several other features that out-class standard Mini-LEDs. They're brighter (far brighter than OLED TVs), making them perfect for daytime watching in bright rooms with little light control. They offer much better viewing angles, which means everyone you're hosting will enjoy the game wherever they're positioned around the TV. Gamers will benefit from this TV as well. The Hisense UR8 boasts a 180Hz native refresh rate, the highest I've ever seen for a TV, with HDMI 2.1 inputs that will pair seamlessly with a PlayStation 5 console for seamlessly running games in 4K.

articles.title: Allisha Gray injury update: Dream All-Star remains 'day-to-day' ahead of WNBA Finals
articles.summary: The availability of Atlanta Dream All-Star guard Allisha Gray is up in the air ahead of Game 1 of the 2026 WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries.
articles.body:
The availability of Atlanta Dream All-Star guard Allisha Gray is up in the air ahead of Game 1 of the 2026 WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries .

Following practice on Thursday, Oct. 15, Gray said she remains "day-to-day" with a left hand injury that she suffered in Game 1 of the Dream's semifinal series win over the New York Liberty on Oct. 4. The four-time All-Star said she's trending in the right direction after undergoing a minor procedure on her injured hand, but the Dream's medical team will have the final say on whether or not she suits up for Saturday's contest.

"Progress has been great, so we're heading in the right direction," Gray told reporters. "Just more so relying on the medical staff. They'll know what's best for me... So it's just taking it day by day, just me getting comfortable, being able to handle the physicality of practice and stuff, which has been feeling well."

The 6-foot guard was a limited participant in Thursday's practice in San Francisco. She participated in shooting drills with black tape holding her left ring finger and pinky finger together. She also appeared to have a bandaid on her left middle finger.

"As long as I can shoot, I'm good," Gray added. "Hopefully I get some good news where I am able to play Saturday."

Liberty, Dream and Aces, Valkyries in WNBA semifinal playoff action

Gray suffered the left hand injury in Game 1 of the Dream's WNBA playoff semifinals series against the New York Liberty on Sunday, Oct. 4. Gray first exited the game holding her left wrist and hand area with 3:59 remaining in the first quarter before returning to the bench at the 9:09 mark of the second quarter with her ring finger and pinky taped. With 3:44 remaining in the first half, Gray dove for a loose ball and appeared to injure the same hand. She left the game and was ruled out before halftime.

"I actually injured it on the first (play)," Gray clarified on Thursday. "Me coming back out was just my competitive nature of not wanting to sit out, but it was just a point where I couldn't play anymore, so I knew that I wasn't able to help my tear anymore, so it was best for me to sit down."

The injury kept Gray out of Game 2 and Game 3 of the semifinal series over the Liberty, which the Dream swept to punch their ticket to the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013.

On Tuesday, Gray revealed she underwent a "minor procedure" on her left hand. Although she didn't disclose the specific procedure, or when she had it, Gray said "everything is put together and fixed. I'm good to go."

The Dream eagerly await the return of Gray, who is averaging 17 points and 1.7 rebounds across three postseason games.

"If we just swept New York with no (Allisha Gray), just imagine what it's going to be like when we bring her back and she's got extra rest," Rhyne Howard said. "She's got an extra week of rest under her belt. The shot's looking good, so it shouldn't be no question about that. But I think once we bring her back, then it's going to be even more unstoppable for us."

Dream guard Allisha Gray is "day-to-day" with a left hand injury.

At the 3:59 mark of the first quarter in Game 1 of a semifinal playoff series, Gray exited holding her left wrist and hand area. Gray was down on the floor for a few moments before being helped up. She went to the locker room for several minutes before returning to the bench at the 9:09 mark of the second quarter. Gray checked back in at the 8:30 mark of the second quarter with two fingers taped (her ring and pinky) on her left hand. She attempted a field goal but missed it. Once she missed the shot, she took off her tape.

Just before halftime, at the 3:44 mark, Gray was diving for a loose basketball on the floor, trying to secure a possession for Atlanta, when she appeared to injure the same hand again. Gray sat on the court, cradling her hand/fingers before going back to the locker room for a second time.

Gray was later ruled out with a left hand injury just before halftime. She returned to the bench after being ruled out, with her left hand heavily wrapped around her ring and pinky fingers. Within the wrap, Gray had a splint on her ring finger.

articles.title: Preorder the SteelSeries Sensei Pro and Rival Pro 8K Gaming Mice With Unlimited Battery Life
articles.summary: Shaping up to be the best gaming mice on the market.
articles.body:
Steelseries recently unveiled a pair of mice that aims to shake up the PC gaming market. The Sensei Pro and Rival Pro , along with its Mini variants, are set to release on November 15 at a launch price of $179.99. New tech doesn't come cheap, but these mice promise to deliver several unique features to justify that hefty price tag. Among them include Steelseries' ingenious hot-swappable battery system for what is essentially unlimited battery life, as well as high-speed ultra wide band connectivity to avoid 2.4GHz congestion.

Preorder the Steelseries Sensei and Rival Pro Gaming Mice

Preorder the Steelseries Sensei Pro Symmetrical Gaming Mouse

Preorder the Steelseries Rival Pro Ergonomic Gaming Mouse

The Sensei Pro and Rival Pro are essentially the same mouse with one primary difference: the Sensei Pro features a symmetrical layout that accommodates both right- and left- handed gamers. The Rival Pro adopts an ergonomic layout that's catered specifically for right-handed users. Both are also available in a "Mini" sized variant for smaller hands.

Amongst the bevy of features packed in the Sensei Pro and Rival Pro, one stands out in particular, and that's the infinite battery system. This is essentially a hot-swappable battery system much like what you'll find in the SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro and Omni headsets, which I consider to be one of the best gaming headets on the market for this reason. The mice basically include two removable, rechargeable batteries: one to use in your mouse and the other to remain charged and ready to go in the base station that doubles as a charger. You won't be constantly swapping during each session either; each battery lasts up to 120 hours on a single charge.

UWB wireless connection avoids 2.4GHz congestion

The Sensei Pro and Rival Pro connect to your PC via ultra wide band wireless (6GHz or higher), thus bypassing the 2.4GHz band that's used by nearly all other wireless peripherals on the market, including headphones, controllers, keyboards, and more. Combined with the hyper-fast 8K polling rate, you're not going to experience any dropouts, stutters, or lag. For gamers who are still married to a wired connection for its reliabilty, this might just be your cue to finally move on.

Pro-grade features and an ultra lightweight body

The new mice don't really compromise on anything else. Quite the opposite, in fact. In addition to the 8K polling rate, the Sensei Pro and Rival Pro are equipped with a TrueMove 42K Pro optical sensor with automatic DPI switching depending on what you're doing (i.e. navigating menus are shooting down your opponents), a total of six programmable buttons that use optical switches rated for 100 million clicks, limitless customization options via Steelseries' GG PC app, pre-applied low friction PTFE feet, and an ultra lightweight design that starts at only 49 grams.

If you're going to spend $180 on a gaming mouse, there can be no doubt in your mind that the mouse you're purchasing is the best of the best. SteelSeries' new entries look fully equipped to occupy that niche.

articles.title: Un hombre instala una PlayStation 5 sin carcasa en una caja de cartón: un año después, su instalación sigue funcionando
articles.standfirst: Una ‘versión’ de la consola de Sony algo sorprendente
articles.summary: Una ‘versión’ de la consola de Sony algo sorprendente
articles.body: Si bien Sony está acostumbrada a sacar a la venta diversos modelos y diseños especiales de sus consolas, lo cierto es que lo ocurrido en Estados Unidos no es nada que la compañía haya decidido, sino que responde a un intento de un hombre por hacer que su PlayStation 5 siguiera funcionando y lo cierto es que, no sin un llamativo diseño, lo ha conseguido y de una manera más que curiosa. Este joven, según explica en Reddit, tiene una tienda de empeños y un día alguien llegó con una PS5 Pro “completamente desarmada”. Al ver ese estado, decidió ofrecerle 100 dólares, pero para quedársela él mismo. Una vez lo hizo, colocó la placa base, la fuente de alimentación y demás componentes necesarios. Pero no lo colocó sobre la carcasa habitual de esta consola, ya que el cliente se lo había dado a Walmart. Así que decidió colocar todos los componentes sobre una caja de cartón y dejó una pequeña abertura para ahí instalar un ventilador. Pese a los comentarios negativos y las burlas, lo cierto es que un año después esa consola sigue funcionando “sin el menor problema”. “Y la uso a diario con las PSVR2, que es la forma más exigente de usar la PS5 Pro”, añade en su historia este joven, que aclara que sin ese ventilador sí acabaría calentándose demasiado debido a la exigencia de juegos como Crimson Desert. Gracias a su maña, este joven ha obtenido una PS5 Pro por apenas 100 dólares, una cifra muy lejana a los 899 dólares que cuesta una consola de estas características en Estados Unidos. Si bien la carcasa apenas le costaría unos 200 dólares, el joven asegura que va a esperar a alguna oferta y, de paso, aprovechar para jugar a GTA 6.

articles.title: Avatar: Seven Havens Continues in Episodes 4-6 With Emotional Hooks and Forward Mythology Momentum
articles.summary: Avatar: Seven Havens Episodes 4-6 recap and review: Pavi and Nisha's story continues as we catalogue Avatar artifacts and more.
articles.body:
Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Avatar: Seven Havens Season 1, Episodes 4-6!

With the next batch of three episodes of Avatar: Seven Havens now on Paramount+, we’re nearly halfway through the first season of the series. The show has clearly hit an episodic rhythm and is amping up the danger for our twin Avatars, Pavi (Saheli Kahn) and Nisha (Aishu Devan), as well as their supposed safe Haven of Ellora. But we’re also still in Ellora, and other than a very menacing red diamond and a group of raiders called the Faceless, it’s curious that we still don’t quite have a sense of what the overall thrust of this story is as of yet.

Okay, that’s not exactly true; the thrust of Book 1: Survival (the overarching name for the season) certainly seems to be Pavi and Nisha regaining the lost memories of their past while the tensions and distrust in Ellora bubble over to unbearable levels, mostly focused on the unseen threat of the Avatar — after all, we’re told it was the previous Avatar, Korra, who broke the world two centuries ago, leading to what’s left of humanity living in Seven Havens.

But the real tense question for viewers watching the show is: When are they going to leave this One (1) Haven and explore the other Six (6) Havens, to make Seven total Havens? Look, it’s gotta happen — probably — but this isn’t the single-city focus that mostly consumed Legend of Korra. There, it made sense to spend a lot of time in Republic City; the steampunk-inspired home for all four types of benders and humans was a vast array of landscapes and social strata. Ellora, by design, is smaller and more in line with where we first met Aang with the Southern Water Tribe before heading off to explore the wide world of Avatar.

In fact, if you look at a similar span of time on The Last Airbender, team Avatar had left the Southern Water Tribe by Episode 6, went to the Southern Air Temple, met the Kyoshi Warriors, headed to the Earth Kingdom of Omashu, and fought the at-the-time villainous Zuko multiple times. Not that Seven Havens needs to ape that formula, but the curiosity factor about the new landscape of the world after Korra’s cataclysm (Korraclysm?) is high. We end Episode 6, “Night of the Afflicted,” with Ellora calling the other Havens for help; however, that likely means the other Havens are coming to Ellora, not Pavi and Nisha going to them.

This would be much less of a problem if every episode didn’t include the twins talking about how they want to go find their parents and see if they’re alive. Yet not once does anyone say, “okay, let’s check outside Ellora,” which is the last place they were seen. Yes, Ellora and its citizens are getting plenty of time in the sun, and they’re all interesting in their own right. But at this point, it feels like Seven Havens is fighting against itself to keep our characters in town instead of following the quest structure the season seemed to be setting up.

Those five paragraphs aside, let’s not also forget that this is a very fun show and a great addition to the Avatar canon. While the season-long view raises some questions about the show’s direction, it’s still lovely to look at on an episode-by-episode basis, adorably funny, and doing a nice job of slowly fleshing out the expansive cast. And thanks to the news out of New York Comic Con that the show will now run at least four seasons, there’s a little bit more breathing room for Seven Havens to stay in Ellora before Pavi, Nisha, and presumably Jae (Major Curda) head out to repair this broken world. When they had just announced two seasons, you could hear the clock ticking away in the background; now, they can hang in Ellora for Season 1 but hopefully get on the road in Seasons 2-4.

Okay, enough long view. To break down the plot more specifically, Episode 4, “The Faceless,” focuses on what seemed to be the big threat last week. As it turns out, they’re really raiders taking grain and other goods from Ellora — late in the episode they kidnap a herd of cameldillos. The smart thing this half-hour does is take this threat and pair it with a very small, personal quest for our three leads to find missing Bending Brigade member Uki (Kimberly Woods). Not only does this allow Pavi to get much weirder, building on her “actually, I talk to rocks and they’re my friends” moment from Episode 3, but it gives us more of a chance to understand the increased fear and panic in Ellora that’s caused or amplified by what was left behind by the red diamond.

Not to compare and contrast two extremely different shows, but take a look at Lanterns over on HBO, which spent a lot of time telling us how nervous the people of the town of Rushville, Nebraska were, while only showing us those people one or two times in eight episodes. Meanwhile, Seven Havens depicts this on multiple levels, from those in the ruling class to citizens in a delicious looking bakery to Uki’s insanely large family, who are worried not just about her but the city itself. As viewers, this gives us a specific emotional tie versus Pavi and Nisha riding their cat-monkeys through a town of, er, faceless nobodies. This storyline is all about panic and fear of the unknown, something extremely relevant to our modern world. The almost-riot in Episode 5, “The One Left Behind,” and the pseudo-zombie attacks in Episode 6, “Night of the Afflicted,” wouldn’t be as effective if we didn’t care about the regular people of Ellora.

And now a quick side-trip to theory town (and scroll down for a very big theory that borders on possible spoilers): We’re all agreed that the Faceless aren’t bad guys; they’re people trying to survive outside the Haven, right? And given the “you should join us” moment at the beginning of the episode, by the time Jae finds Uki again, she’ll understand the Faceless point of view? Okay, cool.

To jump into Episode 5, now that city guard Molin (Osric Chau) is possessed by the red entity and knows (or thinks he knows) the Avatar is in town, tensions are unbearably high. What works nicely about the animation here is that the expressions convey the real pain and terror everyone is feeling as the Guards work to track down the Avatar. Meanwhile, Jae and Bending Brigade Commander Karthik (Akshay Khanna) try to alleviate fears despite knowing there isn’t just one but two Avatars in Ellora.

There’s a lot to like about this episode. Shouts to Seven Havens for doubling down on the relationship between Jae and Datu (Topher Ngo). There’s the funniest moment they’ve had so far, with an old woman responding to Jae’s impassioned pleas with a raspberry, then being haughtily carried away by a large man. And of course, Karthik has a secret closet full of artifacts, aka Avatar easter eggs, which we’ll get into more after the recap. But the biggest plus is again keeping things focused on emotion while spooling out the plot. Here, thanks to a rediscovered bracelet paired with Pavi’s brooch, we discover that Nisha and Pavi’s parents were trying to hide them and contacted the Order of the White Lotus, but when Karthik arrived, he only found Nisha alone in the wasteland. There are strong shades of Rey’s story from Star Wars: The Last Jedi here, though clearly our twin Avatars’ parents know a whole lot more about the world breaking than we’re aware of at the moment.

And then there’s Episode 6, which has Ellora getting its fears amplified by the crystalline structures left behind by the red diamond, with the evil diamond returning not to attack but to show Pavi and Nisha another vision of their mother and father. Perhaps most importantly, Pavi calms down Molin by sticking him in a “cozy wall,” which counts as number two after Raspberry Lady in the list of funniest moments in this batch of episodes. Not to sound like a broken record, but once again this episode pairs the fear zombie plot (the big story) with Pavi’s own fears that she won’t be good enough thanks to the loss of her leg (ostensibly the little story). There’s clearly more to tell there, but the animation conveys her pain and frustration as she tries to help Nisha and Jae quell the madness, and the ultimate delivery of a new prosthetic from an extremely kindly doctor is joyful, as Pavi bounces around the room.

Naturally, the mysteries here — Why are there two Avatars? What’s up with the red diamond? Is it really the wrath of the spirit world, or something else? What about those other six Havens? — are great to theorize about. But as with The Last Airbender and later seasons of The Legend of Korra (they made the mistake of going a little too plot- and exposition-heavy in the first season), the focus is on characters and emotion first .

This does tie neatly into The Big Theory we’ll get into below, and while there is a bit of the “ when are they going to get to the fireworks factory ” in regards to those other Six Havens in this week’s batch of episodes, Seven Havens is doing a bang-up job of making us care not just about Pavi and Nisha, but all of Ellora. There’s a kindness and empathy running through this series that is rare even for animated shows. In short? Avatar: Seven Havens is like sitting inside a nice, cozy wall for 60ish minutes every week.

Avatar Easter Eggs, References, And Connections

Before we get into specific easter eggs, here’s that theory we mentioned — and while it is just a fan theory posted on Reddit , it’s the sort of thing that feels so correct, it may have figured out the whole show after the first week. So possible future spoilers on: The Seven Havens are the Seven Chakras. That’s the short version, but if you don’t recall — back in The Last Airbender Season 2, Aang learned about the seven chakras that, when unlocked, allow him to enter the all-powerful Avatar State. He initially was unable to unlock them due to not letting go of attachments, and was later badly hurt due to Azula’s lightning bending.

Each chakra has a color and an associated emotion, and the colors of the Seven Havens all coincide exactly with the colors of the various chakras. Ellora, you may not be surprised to learn, is depicted as red in the opening credits, and the red chakra or Root Chakra, is blocked by fear. The title of the season finale of Seven Havens’ first season? “The Root Chakra.”

While not exactly “case closed,” the theory continues that Korra either did something or was trying to prevent something from happening (and failed) that broke the chakras of the world. So once Pavi and Nisha figure this out, they won’t be going on a journey to figure out bending à la Aang and Korra since they’ve already mastered all four elements, but rather to unlock the seven chakras of the world and restore balance. The weird weather? That’s because the chakras are blocked; it would also explain why the red diamond isn’t evil. It just needs Pavi and Nisha to do something to unblock Ellora’s fear.

One additional aspect of this theory, by the way, is that intrepid fans have already laid the map of the Seven Havens from the opening credits over the known map of the Avatar world. While some places are unknown or guesses, it seems almost a given that one of the Havens is Ba Sing Se, while the likely final one is none other than Republic City. Again, this makes a lot of sense; if this is indeed a journey to restore the chakras, the place where Korra probably made her last stand would definitely be her home from Legend of Korra.

Is this all true? Just wild guesses? We’ll find out as the show continues, but let’s get into some easter eggs and references we do know for sure.

To work backwards (because pretty much everything we need to talk about is in Episode 5), it’s neat to see lightning bending again, aka the coolest bending. We also get to see Pavi and Nisha do energy bending to “banish” the red diamond, which stuns Karthik. While the above Big Theory seems more plausible, this could throw a little more fire on the “Aang did something when he removed Fire Lord Ozai’s bending” theory, since that also involved energy bending.

Okay, fine, Episode 5. Right at the beginning, we get a fun little mention of “Commander Bountan once told me he saw a dancing lemur-man in the harshlands.” While there’s no way Bountan actually saw this, it’s clear this is a reference to Momo’s iconic dancing in The Last Airbender Season 2, “Tales of Ba Sing Se,” where he danced with some monkeys while trying to find the missing Appa.

…And then Pavi and Nisha end up in Karthik’s secret room, a treasure trove of artifacts collected by the Order of the White Lotus. Look, full disclosure: We’re definitely going to miss things here because there is so much , so sound off in the comments below if you catch something we don’t. But a partial list of artifacts includes:

Sokka’s club, which Pavi uses as a backscratcher and pulls a classic Sokka face as she does

It looks like they might also have Sokka’s sword on one of the higher shelves

The Avatar Relics, aka the toys used to identify Avatars. At the very least, there’s the hand drum, wooden hog monkey, and pull-string propeller used with Aang seen in the foreground as Nisha enters the room

The map of the world as seen in the opening title sequence of The Last Airbender

Zuko’s Blue Spirit mask from when he went undercover as a vigilante

Nisha picks up an object with the three swirls indicating the Air Nation

There’s a musical instrument on the wall that, shapewise, looks closest to Chong’s instrument — the dramyin — from The Last Airbender Season 2’s “The Cave of Two Lovers”

Any radios are going to be from the Legend of Korra era, since the tech hadn’t been developed in the time of The Last Airbender. It’s possible one of these might be Bumi’s portable radio, or based on it in some way

As Pavi accidentally turns on the radio and becomes terrified, we see a red umbrella, which is likely the same one Aang got as a present in The Last Airbender Season 1, Episode 14, “The Fortuneteller”

The “lantern” Pavi excitedly calls out definitely seems to be something, so feel free to make fun of us for not figuring out what it is; same for the purple robe with long sleeves in the back, which looks like something Princess Yue would wear but is not. Probably. Regardless, there’s a lot there to freeze frame and comb through, and it makes sense that they wouldn’t have many relics from Korra’s era since they, you know, hate Korra.

articles.title: Mike Flanagan Explains Why Warhammer 40,000 Is a 'Brutally Difficult Adaptation'
articles.summary: Mike Flanagan has discussed the challenges of adapting Warhammer 40,000 into an Amazon TV series, calling it “brutally difficult.”
articles.body:
Mike Flanagan has discussed the challenges of adapting Warhammer 40,000 into an Amazon TV series, calling it “brutally difficult.”

Flanagan, writer, director and showrunner of a number of much-loved Netflix horror TV shows including The Haunting of Hill House, The Haunting of Bly Manor, and The Fall of the House of Usher, has signed a multi-year deal with Amazon to develop and produce original series for the studio. The first of these is an adaptation of Stephen King’s horror classic, Carrie, which recently hit Prime Video. Next up is a Warhammer 40,000 TV show, which will be part of Henry Cavill’s Warhammer 40,000 Cinematic Universe. The former Superman actor is set to star in the show.

Meanwhile, Flanagan has another project many fans can’t wait for him to get to: The Dark Tower. But this adaptation of Stephen King’s much-loved fantasy saga sounds even further away. Indeed, Flanagan admitted over the summer that he’s having a tough time getting a green light for The Dark Tower , despite the fact it’s relatively straight forward in his head.

Warhammer 40,000 11th Edition Cinematic Trailer: All Shots of the Emperor

Warhammer 40,000, however, is not. Speaking on The Process Unlocked , Flanagan explained why adapting Warhammer 40,000 is so much tougher than The Dark Tower.

“I'll tell you, I feel like I'm climbing my adaptation Everest right now, because I've been working — and this is out there so I can talk just barely a little bit about it — but I've been working on Warhammer,” he began.

Flanagan’s approach to adapting The Dark Tower is, straightforwardly, to adapt King’s books in order. “That one I feel like I figured out,” he said. "You do the books.

“Stephen King is genius in how he structures The Dark Tower because he starts this giant worldbuilding potentially, overwhelming story with two people in a landscape without detail. It's the simplest start,” he continued. “It's one of the most perfect lines of any book: 'The man in black fled across the desert and the gunslinger followed.' It is two characters. There's a clear objective. One is running away, one is pursuing, and it's a desert. There is nothing else to look at. It's so simple and so clean and on top of that foundation, he adds a universe one brick at a time.

“And so that's the way to do it. The problem with the other approaches is people who try to jump in in the middle or people who try to jump in at a different point, because you can't throw an audience face first into this huge universe. It's overwhelming. And King did it right. He walked you in, started with two people and nothing else and walks you in one step at a time. So my adaptation was that, it was just doing the books and doing them in order. And there's little changes you make to fit the the format, but my Dark Tower approach is remarkably faithful. And so 70% of my job is done for me by Steve. So it's not that difficult. You know, the difficult thing is just figuring out how to get in.

Flanagan then went on to point out that the Warhammer 40,000 universe has 700 novels to its name, compared to eight for The Dark Tower. It is a bewildering backstory to build from.

“These are novel length,” he said of the Warhammer 40,000 novels. “These are not small. But there are so many characters. It takes place over so many thousands of years. There's so much there. The challenge is how do you get in? That's really a brutally difficult adaptation, but it's been so fun for it.”

It’s true: there are hundreds, and hundreds, and hundreds of official, full-length Warhammer 40,000 novels, produced by Games Workshop’s book business, Black Library. They tell the stories that underpin the tabletop game’s “grim darkness of the far future” setting, touching on everything from the machinations of chaos gods to the trials and tribulations of downtrodden humans. The 41st millennium is an overwhelming setting, one that has become dense with lore over the course of decades. And not much of it makes a great deal of sense, either. Fans must remind themselves, as the unreliable Warhammer 40,000 canon marches on inexorably, that each tale they devour is only delivered from a certain point of view. Indeed, the Emperor himself is perhaps the most unknowable being in the galaxy .

This is why you often see newcomers ask grizzled veterans for a starting point when it comes to Warhammer 40,000 novels. Dan Abnett’s wonderful Eisenhorn series is a popular recommendation, as it follows the inquisitors Gregor Eisenhorn and Gideon Ravenor on a relatively grounded detective story. From there, perhaps dip your toe into the bigger picture moves of the likes of Ultramarines primarch Roboute Guilliman, or dare to delve deep into the foundational Horus Heresy. But whatever you do, don’t force it. Who knows what truly resides in the darkest corners of the lore?

This is Flanagan’s challenge, then: how do you create a Warhammer 40,000 series when the Warhammer 40,000 universe has no obvious entry point? How do you make something accessible for newcomers when you’re adapting a universe that has no real beginning, middle, or end?

I keep coming back to Eisenhorn. Indeed I think Henry Cavill will play Eisenhorn in the Warhammer 40,000 TV show. I wrote about why extensively earlier this year . In short, author Dan Abnett has sort of suggested the series has something to do with Amazon... stuff, and he's sitting on the latest entry while he waits for Games Workshop and everyone else involved to get their ducks in a row.

An Eisenhorn adaptation would, theoretically at least, be tighter in scope than some of the grander Warhammer 40,000 stories, and help keep production manageable. The Eisenhorn Omnibus series does feature Space Marines, but they only make brief and rare appearances. The story focuses heavily on Gregor Eisenhorn and regular humans rather than the giant genetically enhanced warriors.

Hopefully it won’t be too long until we find out.

Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: Humble’s Cozy After Dark Showcase Bundle Is Perfect for Halloween, With 10 Spooky Indie Games for $12
articles.summary: Humble Bundle's Cozy After Dark Showcase bundle features 10 wonderfully spooky indie games you can grab for as low as $12, including Fear the Spotlight, Paradise Killer, and more.
articles.body:
Nothing beats jumping into a scary game around Halloween. But if you're someone who prefers games on the lighter side of spooky, Humble's Cozy After Dark Showcase Bundle is perfect for you. This collection of 10 eerie indies is available to grab for as low as $12, and features a great lineup that includes Paradise Killer and Fear the Spotlight .

If you were to buy all 10 of these games on their own, it'd set you back $176, so this is a fantastic offer to take advantage of. As of the time of writing, it's only available for another 18 days as well, so the countdown is on to grab it. Below, you can check out the full game lineup for this bundle, which can all be redeemed on Steam if you decide to treat yourself to it.

Humble Bundle – Cozy After Dark Showcase Bundle

If really scary games aren't for you, this bundle is full of some great options that can bring you that spooky season atmosphere in a lighter fashion. Fear the Spotlight is one that I really enjoyed, which is a delightful love letter to PS1-era horror games and Blumhouse Games' debut launch.

There's also Paradise Killer, which is one writer Joe Skrebels gave a 9/10 to in his review , writing that it "marries a beautifully repulsive world with a gratifyingly open-ended approach to detective work, but its real achievement is in how it ties everything you’ve learned together."

If you don't want to pay the full $12 for all these games, though, there's some slight changes to the bundle. Dropping down to $8, the lowest amount, will net you five games instead of the full 10: Paradise Killer, Escape From Mystwood Mansion, a pet shop after dark, The Darkside Detective, and Kathy Rain Directors Cut.

And if you'd like to pay a bit extra instead, you'll be giving more money to publishers, Humble, and charity alongside getting the full set of 10 games. The charity for this bundle is Dames4Games as well, which supports women and femme-identifying people across gaming and tech.

Hannah Hoolihan is a freelancer who writes with the commerce team here at IGN.

articles.title: Rockstar Mods Real Life Vehicles to Look Like GTA 6 Cars Before Driving Them Through Miami
articles.summary: Rockstar’s wild marketing push for GTA 6 is well underway, with the latest seeing modded cars cruising around Miami.
articles.body:
Rockstar’s wild marketing push for GTA 6 is well underway, with the latest seeing modded cars cruising around Miami. The GTA 6 developer pimped out some real-world vehicles to look like their in-game counterparts and showed them off around The Magic City.

The cars rocked Leonida license plates — the plates you’ll see in the game’s fictionalized Florida — and drove around in a tight convoy, with a VCPD-liveried Lamborghini police vehicle in the mix. There was also a McLaren, kitted out to look like a real life Progen Emerus.

Other looks included real-life takes on the Cheetah, the Coquette D10, the Tempesta, and the Manana. I can’t even imagine how much this cost to put together.

Rockstar Games appear to be marketing #GTAVI in Miami with a street car showcase, featuring Leonida licence plates and a VCPD-liveried Lamborghini 👀 Sources: / @WillMacGTA — ben (@videotech) October 16, 2026

Rockstar Games appear to be marketing #GTAVI in Miami with a street car showcase, featuring Leonida licence plates and a VCPD-liveried Lamborghini 👀 Sources: / @WillMacGTA

“That Vice City Police Huracan is FIRE,” said one X / Twitter user . “Miami is so unserious for turning a game launch into a city-wide event like this is just a normal Tuesday for them,” said another .

Sentiment across social media is mostly positive, with players impressed by the creativity of GTA 6’s launch marketing. So far, it’s definitely been a step up from what we usually see from triple-A studios, and more over the top than any movie promotion I can remember in recent years.

Local news page Only in Dade got a look at some of the vehicles parked up at a gas station as the Goodyear blimp, featuring its own GTA 6 advertisement, hovered in the distance. PlayStation reminding players GTA 5 is leaving PS Plus soon kinda pales in comparison.

Rockstar developers traveled across Florida on GTA 6 research trips to portray the state as authentically as possible in its satire-laden recreation of Miami and the surrounding areas. CBS news recently did a segment on GTA 6 , astonished by how accurately the game captures the city.

Elsewhere, the Australian government put out a graphic that informed citizens of their rights for requesting time off work when GTA 6 launches next month. All while Rockstar has been taking over Miami in its big marketing push leading up to launch.

Some Miami officials have expressed concern over the studio’s influence, with Rockstar taking over beaches and collaborating with local NBA team the Miami Heat . The marketing machine is at full tilt now, right up to when GTA 6 launches for PS5 and Xbox Series consoles on November 19.

It's been a busy week for GTA 6. We've got a report on what sounds like the end of Cyberleek , details of GTA 6’s sweat system , and confirmation GTA 6 is eligible for The Game Awards 2026 .

articles.title: The Dark Tower TV Series Would Be 'Remarkably Faithful' to Stephen King's Books, Mike Flanagan Says
articles.summary: Mike Flanagan has revealed his approach for the hotly-anticipated The Dark Tower TV show, which is sure to please fans of Stephen King’s book series.
articles.body:
Mike Flanagan has revealed his approach for the hotly-anticipated The Dark Tower TV show, which is sure to please fans of Stephen King’s book series.

Flanagan, famous for Netflix horror shows The Haunting of Hill House, The Haunting of Bly Manor, and, most recently, Amazon's Carrie, has been trying to get an adaptation of King’s much-loved fantasy saga off the ground for years — despite the fact the script for Season 1 has King’s seal of approval.

The Dark Tower is currently “one of the most complicated properties to get started,” Flanagan told Entertainment Weekly in the summer, referencing his struggle to get the go-ahead . “Getting the green light on Dark Tower is a much longer and more involved process than anything else I’ve ever approached in my life.”

The Essentials: Stephen King's Dark Tower Multiverse

Actually getting The Dark Tower made is the hard part, then. But in terms of the adaptation itself, it’s relatively straightforward. That’s because Flanagan has taken the approach of faithfully adapting the books, almost to a fault, leaning heavily on the story King himself told.

“That one I feel like I figured out,” Flanagan said in a recent interview with The Process Unlocked . "You do the books.”

That sounds obvious, but it is not the path previous The Dark Tower adaptations have followed — much to the disappointment of fans. The 2017 movie, starring Idris Elba as Roland Deschain and Matthew McConaughey as his nemesis, Walter Padick, was panned by critics. Flanagan has said of the film: “We can’t let that be the final word. We really can’t.”

The big idea, Flanagan has said, is for five seasons of The Dark Tower followed by two standalone movies. Or, put more simply by Flanagan in this new interview: “just doing the books and doing them in order.”

“Stephen King is genius in how he structures The Dark Tower because he starts this giant worldbuilding potentially, overwhelming story with two people in a landscape without detail. It's the simplest start,” Flanagan explained.

“It's one of the most perfect lines of any book: 'The man in black fled across the desert and the gunslinger followed.' It is two characters. There's a clear objective. One is running away, one is pursuing, and it's a desert. There is nothing else to look at. It's so simple and so clean and on top of that foundation, he adds a universe one brick at a time.

“And so that's the way to do it. The problem with the other approaches is people who try to jump in in the middle or people who try to jump in at a different point, because you can't throw an audience face first into this huge universe. It's overwhelming. And King did it right. He walked you in, started with two people and nothing else and walks you in one step at a time. So my adaptation was that, it was just doing the books and doing them in order. And there's little changes you make to fit the the format, but my Dark Tower approach is remarkably faithful. And so 70% of my job is done for me by Steve. So it's not that difficult. You know, the difficult thing is just figuring out how to get in.”

The question is, will Flanagan get the chance to realize his vision? The Dark Tower is not a part of Flanagan’s big Amazon deal, although he has suggested Prime Video could get behind it eventually. Next up for the horror specialist is an Amazon TV show adaptation of Warhammer 40,000, which he’s said is much harder to adapt than The Dark Tower .

So while Flanagan’s plan for The Dark Tower sounds great, if it ever does come to pass, it will be many years from now.

articles.title: MTG's New Foundations Commander Decks Return to Online Retailers After Stock Shortages
articles.summary: Magic: The Gathering's new 2026 Foundations Commander decks have returned to major retailers after shortages online post-launch in early October.
articles.body:
Magic: The Gathering's new Foundations Commander decks are back in stock at major online retailers, including Amazon, after shortages since their arrival alongside Reality Fracture .

The five decks arrived on October 2, 2026, giving players an accessible way to get started with Commander , MTG's most popular multiplayer format. Each deck is super affordable, with a different mono-color strategy built around a familiar creature type or playstyle, from Angels and Dragons to Dinosaurs, Zombies, and artifacts.

MTG’s Foundation Decks Are Almost All Back In Stock

It’s worth noting right off the bat that, sadly, the price has crept up on some of these precons. Despite an MSRP of $30, they’ve been climbing a little due to months of intermittent stock shortages for preorders and since launch at the start of October.

Yet, despite this, there are still some fairly good deals up for grabs when you compare prices to current market rates at TCGplayer. For example, Reign of Dragons (the mono-red deck) is available for $35.44 at Amazon right now, while the zombie-focused mono-black deck, Wretched Ranks , is $39.99. Wretched Ranks matches its market rates, but Reign of the Dragons is considerably less than its average price of $47.68 at TCGplayer right now.

Keen Engineering , the artifact-heavy mono-blue precon, on the other hand, is up to $43.07, but we expect that to drop swiftly — it’s the only deck that was often being sold for under MSRP in recent weeks, and a current market price of $30.26 at TCGplayer.

The best deal, however, is undoubtedly on Calling All Angels . The very fun (and pretty powerful) mono-white Angels deck, is back in stock at $29.99 (MSRP), and $22 below its current market average of $52.

Pricing are still trending up for these decks at the moment, with the five deck bundle reaching average prices of around $195, over $45 above the MSRP of $149.95.

That's an average of $39 per deck, which isn't entirely terrible, but I'd encourage you to buy the single decks, or wait it out a bit longer for prices to come down again. The closer you can get to the intended list price of $30 per deck, the better.

Tramplesaurus Rex, the mono-green deck based around dinosaurs, isn’t back in stock yet. That means it’s climbing on the secondary market, buoyed by reprints of cards like Surrak and Goreclaw.

We’re seeing it reach $60 on the likes of TCGplayer , and as fun as it’ll be to overpower your foes with big dinos, it’s simply not worth paying double the price for.

We’re expecting Wizards of the Coast to reprint these decks regularly since they have the Foundations title attached to them, meaning players will have an easier way to jump into the format.

Once they do, expect all of these decks, including the green one, to dip when that happens. So keep an eye out for that!

Foundations is an ideal starting point for new players — or for those of us looking to share the Commander format with friends or family.

Calling All Angels is a mono-white Angels typal deck, helmed by Giada, Font of Hope. Reign of Dragons is a mono-red Dragon deck starring Lathliss, Dragon Queen, while Tramplesaurus Rex will ramp quickly to bring out big dinosaurs like its Commander, Ghalta, Primal Hunger.

Then there’s Ghoulcaller Gisa, who helms the mono-black zombie/sacrifice deck Wretched Ranks , and finally, Sai, Master Thopterist, whose mono-blue deck, Keen Engineering , is all about artifacts.

These are all well-worn playstyles, but the point here is the cohesion rather than the competitiveness. These decks are easy to hand to a friend over the holidays and say “let’s play a game”, while also giving them a little bit of guidance towards their preferred playstyle.

For more on Magic: The Gathering, be sure to check out Reality Fracture’s priciest cards , as well as all we know about the Warhammer 40K Commander decks seeing a reprint .

Robert Anderson is a Senior Commerce Editor for IGN. Based in London, UK, he is a qualified journalist with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism (First Class Degree) and over seven years of professional writing and editing experience.

You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.

His primary coverage focuses on tracking down the best gaming deals and diving into the fast-paced world of Trading Card Games (TCGs). He regularly covers everything from the latest releases in Pokémon TCG and the most expensive cards to comprehensive Magic: The Gathering buying guides .

articles.title: Here's Our First Look at Dark Link in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake
articles.summary: Nintendo has shown off Dark Link in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for the first time.
articles.body:
As Nintendo has pulled back the curtain on The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake , we’ve begun to get a better understanding of how this Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive will look and feel to play. IGN has already got you covered with an extensive hands-on preview , as well as a roundup of all the changes we’ve noticed so far compared to the N64 masterpiece.

But now, Nintendo has released two new trailers (TV spots for Japan) that, while brief, reveal a tantalizing glimpse at some never-before-seen characters, chief among them Dark Link.

[任天堂HP]Nintendo Switch 2 ソフト『ゼルダの伝説 時のオカリナ』のCMを公開しました。 #時のオカリナ #ゼルダの伝説40周年 — 任天堂株式会社 (@Nintendo) October 16, 2026

[任天堂HP]Nintendo Switch 2 ソフト『ゼルダの伝説 時のオカリナ』のCMを公開しました。 #時のオカリナ #ゼルダの伝説40周年

Warning! Potential spoilers for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake follow…

Fans of the original game will know Dark Link well. He’s a shadowy, mirror-image doppelgänger of Link who serves as the mini-boss of Ocarina’s iconic Water Temple. You fight him in a fog-filled room with shallow water and a dead tree in the center, in what is one of the more memorable battles in the game. Brilliantly, Dark Link’s name mirrors the player's save file name (as registered by Navi), and his total health scales dynamically to match the exact number of Heart Containers Link has at that moment.

The new trailer shows this fight in action, although we only get the briefest of looks at how it plays out. We see Dark Link leak onto Link’s sword, looking down menacingly at our hero.

Dark Link isn’t the only thing worth highlighting about these two videos. We see big bad guy Ganondorf playing an organ, Link playing his Ocarina, the cutscene where Link finally gets the Master Sword, and plenty more.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Preview Screenshots

Indeed, I’d say these trailers veer into spoiler territory if you’ve never played Ocarina of Time before, which is why I’ve slapped this article with a spoiler warning up top. As a huge fan of the original game, there isn’t really anything here that would spoil my enjoyment, but we do see some endgame footage.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches on Nintendo Switch 2 on November 5, 2026. While you wait, check out a special episode of Nintendo Voice Chat where we dive deeper into our Zelda preview.
